# Rise and Battle the Day
## Scripture
"Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go." – Joshua 1:9
## Reflection
Every morning you wake up, a battle is already waiting. Not against flesh and blood, but against complacency, distraction, and the quiet pull to drift through another day on autopilot. Joshua stood at the edge of the promised land facing giants, walled cities, and his own fear—and God didn't coddle him. He commanded him: be strong and courageous. Notice the reason God gives. Not "because you're tough enough," but "because I am with you." Your courage was never meant to rest on your own shoulders. It rests on the presence of the God who goes before you. That means you can step into today—into hard conversations, hard work, and hard choices—without being paralyzed by fear. Courage is not the absence of fear; it's obedience in the presence of it. So before your feet hit the floor, decide who you're fighting for. Men of God don't wait for the battle to feel manageable. They rise, they trust, and they move.
## Daily Challenge
Do 25 pushups—one for each verse in the first chapter of Joshua—and with every rep, declare: "The Lord my God is with me."
